title: Silent for Four Days, Now It Speaks for Free | vitalii.no
description:
Why a daily video digest went mute for four days, and how switching its Norwegian narration to a free voice engine fixed two problems at once.

The digest's Norwegian narration ran through a paid text-to-speech reseller, whose two voices were actually resold Microsoft neural voices under different names. When the reseller's account balance ran out, every digest render died at the exact same voiceover step, and it stayed broken for four days because nothing upstream could tell the difference between an empty balance and a genuinely broken API.

The fix speaks to Microsoft's free Edge TTS endpoint directly, in the same two voices, for nothing — cutting the paid reseller out of the chain entirely. It also solves a second, unrelated problem along the way: the reseller's word-timing endpoint was never available on this account, so subtitle timings for the digest's animated captions had only ever been guessed from gaps of silence in the audio. Edge TTS instead emits a real timing event per spoken word, so the voiceover generator now reads exact, measured timings straight from those events instead of inferring them.

The narration no longer depends on a paid account staying funded, subtitle timing is now measured instead of guessed, and after four days of every render failing at this exact step, the pipeline runs again.
